note: Hand-authored per-sentence analysis for the Wanneer topic: time clauses, direct questions and indirect questions. Status ai-editorial-checked is not native-speaker review.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: The call happens at a moment tied to arriving home, a future time that is not yet fixed, so 'wanneer' fits.

pat-wanneer-01.situationNl: Je gaat straks naar huis en een vriend wacht op bericht. Beloof hem een telefoontje op een bepaald punt van je avond.

clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so 'bel' is second and the object 'je' follows; the clause is complete without the time clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The predicate 'thuis' stands before the finite verb 'ben', which closes the clause.

pat-wanneer-01.meaning: I'll call you when I'm home.
pat-wanneer-01.order: The promise comes first with ordinary order, then the time clause follows with 'ben' last. The present tense carries the future.
pat-wanneer-01.forms: bellen: ik bel. zijn: ik ben. 'Thuis zijn' = to be at home. 'Wanneer' here equals 'als'; both can open a future time clause.
pat-wanneer-01.compare: English 'when I'm home' also uses the present for the future. Dutch moves the verb 'ben' to the end.

mistakes.wrong: Ik bel je wanneer ik ben thuis.
mistakes.right: Ik bel je wanneer ik thuis ben.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'ben' goes behind the predicate 'thuis' at the end of the clause.

mistakes.wrong: Ik bel je wanneer ik thuis ben je.
mistakes.right: Ik bel je wanneer ik thuis ben.
mistakes.why: The pronoun 'je' belongs to the main clause, directly behind 'bel'.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer ik thuis ben, bel ik je.
contrast.english: When I'm home, I'll call you.
contrast.note: Moving the time clause first makes the main clause invert to 'bel ik'.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: The document will be sent once you are ready: a future time clause that opens the sentence.

pat-wanneer-02.situationNl: Een collega wacht op de afgewerkte versie van je tekst. Je zit er nog middenin. Geef aan op welk punt hij het ontvangt.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The predicate 'klaar' stands before the finite verb 'ben', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so the finite verb 'stuur' comes first and the subject 'ik' follows with the object 'het document'.

pat-wanneer-02.meaning: When I'm ready, I'll send the document.
pat-wanneer-02.order: Opening with the time clause puts the emphasis on the moment. The main clause then has verb, subject, object, with the promise as its content.
pat-wanneer-02.forms: zijn: ik ben. sturen: ik stuur. 'Document' is a het-word.
pat-wanneer-02.compare: English 'I'll send' marks the future with 'will'. Dutch keeps the present 'stuur'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer ik ben klaar, stuur ik het document.
mistakes.right: Wanneer ik klaar ben, stuur ik het document.
mistakes.why: The finite verb belongs behind the predicate 'klaar'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer ik klaar ben, ik stuur het document.
mistakes.right: Wanneer ik klaar ben, stuur ik het document.
mistakes.why: After the opening clause the main clause starts with its verb: 'stuur ik'.

contrast.dutch: Ik stuur het document wanneer ik klaar ben.
contrast.english: I'll send the document when I'm ready.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the subject leads and no inversion occurs.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: The start of the lesson depends on the teacher's entrance, a general rule rather than a past event.

pat-wanneer-03.situationNl: Een leerling komt te vroeg en vraagt wat het teken voor de start van de lessen is. Leg uit welke gebeurtenis het begin markeert.

clauses.subject: De les
clauses.why: 'De les' is first, so 'begint' is second; the clause is complete without the time clause.

clauses.subject: de docent
clauses.why: The subject 'de docent' comes first and the joined separable verb 'binnenkomt' closes the clause.

pat-wanneer-03.meaning: The lesson begins when the teacher comes in.
pat-wanneer-03.order: A general statement about a routine. The separable verb 'binnenkomen' is written as one word in the dependent clause.
pat-wanneer-03.forms: beginnen: de les begint. binnenkomen: komt binnen (main clause), binnenkomt (dependent clause). 'Docent' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-03.compare: English 'comes in' stays split. Dutch joins the particle to the verb at the end of the clause.

mistakes.wrong: De les begint wanneer de docent komt binnen.
mistakes.right: De les begint wanneer de docent binnenkomt.
mistakes.why: In a wanneer-clause the separable verb is written as one word: 'binnenkomt'.

mistakes.wrong: De les wanneer de docent binnenkomt begint.
mistakes.right: De les begint wanneer de docent binnenkomt.
mistakes.why: The time clause follows the main clause here; 'begint' stays in second place.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer de docent binnenkomt, begint de les.
contrast.english: When the teacher comes in, the lesson begins.
contrast.note: With the time clause first, the main clause inverts to 'begint de les'.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: The discussion of results follows the end of the meeting; a planned, future sequence.

pat-wanneer-04.situationNl: Het overleg loopt uit en iedereen wil de uitkomsten kennen. Zeg wat jullie met de hele groep doen aan het einde van de bijeenkomst.

clauses.subject: de vergadering
clauses.role: time clause (the end of the meeting)
clauses.why: The participle 'afgelopen' stands before the finite verb 'is', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'bespreken' comes first and the subject 'we' follows with the object.

pat-wanneer-04.meaning: When the meeting finishes, we discuss the results.
pat-wanneer-04.order: 'Afgelopen zijn' (to be over) is a state, so the clause uses 'is'. The plan in the main clause uses the present for the future.
pat-wanneer-04.forms: aflopen > afgelopen. bespreken: wij bespreken. 'Resultaten' is plural.
pat-wanneer-04.compare: English 'finishes' is a simple verb. Dutch often says the meeting 'is afgelopen' (is over).

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de vergadering afgelopen, bespreken we de resultaten.
mistakes.right: Wanneer de vergadering afgelopen is, bespreken we de resultaten.
mistakes.why: The time clause needs its finite verb 'is' at the end; the participle 'afgelopen' alone is not a clause.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de vergadering afgelopen is, we bespreken de resultaten.
mistakes.right: Wanneer de vergadering afgelopen is, bespreken we de resultaten.
mistakes.why: After the opening clause the main clause starts with its verb: 'bespreken we'.

contrast.dutch: We bespreken de resultaten wanneer de vergadering afgelopen is.
contrast.english: We discuss the results when the meeting finishes.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the subject 'we' leads.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: The update will arrive at a future moment, so you promise to inform the colleague then.

pat-wanneer-05.situationNl: Een collega vraagt hoe lang het archiveren nog duurt. Je weet het niet precies. Beloof hem een berichtje op het goede moment.

clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so 'laat' is second; 'het je' are the objects and 'weten' the infinitive that completes 'laten weten'.

clauses.subject: de back-up
clauses.why: The predicate 'klaar' stands before the finite verb 'is', which closes the clause.

pat-wanneer-05.meaning: I'll let you know when the backup is ready.
pat-wanneer-05.order: 'Laten weten' (let know) is a fixed pair: 'laat' second, 'weten' at the end of the main clause. The time clause then follows.
pat-wanneer-05.forms: laten weten: ik laat weten. zijn: de back-up is. 'Back-up' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-05.compare: English 'I'll let you know' uses 'will'. Dutch uses the present 'laat ... weten'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik laat het je weten wanneer de back-up is klaar.
mistakes.right: Ik laat het je weten wanneer de back-up klaar is.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'is' belongs behind the predicate 'klaar'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik laat weten het je wanneer de back-up klaar is.
mistakes.right: Ik laat het je weten wanneer de back-up klaar is.
mistakes.why: The objects 'het je' stand before the infinitive 'weten'.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer de back-up klaar is, laat ik het je weten.
contrast.english: When the backup is ready, I'll let you know.
contrast.note: Time clause first: the main clause inverts to 'laat ik het je weten'.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: Boarding happens at a future moment, tied to the train's arrival.

pat-wanneer-06.situationNl: Jullie staan op een rustig perron en de treinen zijn laat. Vertel wat jullie doen op het punt dat het voertuig stopt.

clauses.subject: de trein
clauses.why: The joined separable verb 'aankomt' closes the clause behind the subject 'de trein'.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'stappen' comes first, then 'we', and the particle 'in' ends the clause.

pat-wanneer-06.meaning: When the train arrives, we board.
pat-wanneer-06.order: 'Instappen' splits in the main clause: 'stappen ... in'. The particle stands at the very end, after the subject 'we'.
pat-wanneer-06.forms: aankomen: komt aan / aankomt. instappen: stappen in. 'Trein' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-06.compare: English 'board' is a single verb. Dutch uses the separable verb 'instappen'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de trein komt aan, stappen we in.
mistakes.right: Wanneer de trein aankomt, stappen we in.
mistakes.why: The separable verb is written together in the wanneer-clause.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de trein aankomt, we stappen in.
mistakes.right: Wanneer de trein aankomt, stappen we in.
mistakes.why: The main clause starts with its verb: 'stappen we in'.

contrast.dutch: We stappen in wanneer de trein aankomt.
contrast.english: We board when the train arrives.
contrast.note: With the main clause first the particle 'in' stays inside the main clause.

sense.label: wanneer = when (question word)
sense.why: A direct question: 'wanneer' asks for a time, so the verb follows it immediately.

pat-wanneer-07.situationNl: Je staat bij een halte zonder bord met tijden. Vraag een voorbijganger naar het uur van de volgende rit.

clauses.subject: de bus
clauses.why: 'Wanneer' opens the question, so the finite verb 'vertrekt' is second and the subject 'de bus' follows it.

pat-wanneer-07.order: No subordinate clause: question word, verb, subject. This is the shape of every direct wanneer-question, here with a short noun-phrase subject.
pat-wanneer-07.forms: vertrekken: de bus vertrekt. 'Bus' is a de-word. 'Wanneer' asks for a time or a date.
pat-wanneer-07.compare: English needs the auxiliary 'does'. Dutch just places the finite verb directly after the question word.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de bus vertrekt?
mistakes.right: Wanneer vertrekt de bus?
mistakes.why: In a direct question the verb comes right after 'wanneer'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer vertrekt bus de?
mistakes.right: Wanneer vertrekt de bus?
mistakes.why: The article stays with its noun: 'de bus'.

contrast.dutch: Ik weet niet wanneer de bus vertrekt.
contrast.english: I don't know when the bus leaves.
contrast.note: In an indirect question the same words reorder so that 'vertrekt' goes last.

sense.label: wanneer = when (question word)
sense.why: A direct question about a start date; the verb follows the question word.

pat-wanneer-08.situationNl: Een goede vriend heeft net een sollicitatie gewonnen. Vraag hem naar de eerste werkdag.

clauses.subject: je nieuwe baan
clauses.why: 'Wanneer' opens the question, so the finite verb 'begint' is second and the subject 'je nieuwe baan' follows it.

pat-wanneer-08.meaning: When does your new job start?
pat-wanneer-08.order: The subject is a noun phrase after the verb. The adjective 'nieuwe' takes -e after the possessive 'je', and 'begint' follows 'wanneer' directly.
pat-wanneer-08.forms: beginnen: de baan begint. 'Baan' is a de-word, so 'je nieuwe baan'.
pat-wanneer-08.compare: English 'does ... start' needs 'does'. Dutch inverts verb and subject without it.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer je nieuwe baan begint?
mistakes.right: Wanneer begint je nieuwe baan?
mistakes.why: The verb comes right after the question word: 'Wanneer begint'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer begint je nieuw baan?
mistakes.right: Wanneer begint je nieuwe baan?
mistakes.why: After a possessive the adjective takes -e: 'nieuwe'.

contrast.dutch: Weet je wanneer je nieuwe baan begint?
contrast.english: Do you know when your new job starts?
contrast.note: Embedded after 'weet je', the verb moves to the end.

sense.label: wanneer = when (question word)
sense.why: A direct question with a modal: the finite verb 'kunnen' follows 'wanneer'.

pat-wanneer-09.situationNl: Het team wil de aanpassing uitproberen voor ze live gaat. Vraag je IT-collega's naar een geschikt tijdstip.

clauses.text: Wanneer kunnen we de wijziging testen
clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: 'Wanneer' opens the question, so the modal 'kunnen' is second, followed by 'we', the object and the infinitive 'testen'.

pat-wanneer-09.meaning: When can we test the change?
pat-wanneer-09.order: The modal stays second and the infinitive goes to the end: 'kunnen ... testen'. The object stands between subject and infinitive.
pat-wanneer-09.forms: kunnen: wij kunnen. testen: infinitive after a modal. 'Wijziging' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-09.compare: English 'can we test' has the same chain. Dutch keeps the infinitive at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer we kunnen de wijziging testen?
mistakes.right: Wanneer kunnen we de wijziging testen?
mistakes.why: The verb 'kunnen' comes directly after 'wanneer'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer kunnen we testen de wijziging?
mistakes.right: Wanneer kunnen we de wijziging testen?
mistakes.why: The object goes before the infinitive at the end.

contrast.dutch: Kunnen we de wijziging testen?
contrast.english: Can we test the change?
contrast.note: Without the question word the verb comes first, giving a yes/no question.

sense.label: wanneer = when (question word)
sense.why: A direct question with 'moeten': the modal follows 'wanneer'.

pat-wanneer-10.situationNl: Je moet papieren afgeven aan de balie van de administratie. Vraag een medewerker welke dag de laatste is.

clauses.text: Wanneer moet ik het formulier inleveren
clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: 'Wanneer' opens the question, so the modal 'moet' is second, then 'ik', the object and the infinitive 'inleveren'.

pat-wanneer-10.meaning: When do I have to submit the form?
pat-wanneer-10.order: The modal 'moet' stays second and the separable infinitive 'inleveren' stays whole at the very end, after the subject and the object.
pat-wanneer-10.forms: moeten: ik moet. inleveren: infinitive (separable, not split after a modal). 'Formulier' is a het-word.
pat-wanneer-10.compare: English 'do I have to submit' uses 'do'. Dutch has none and keeps 'moet' next to 'wanneer'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer ik moet het formulier inleveren?
mistakes.right: Wanneer moet ik het formulier inleveren?
mistakes.why: The modal comes directly after 'wanneer'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer moet ik het formulier leveren in?
mistakes.right: Wanneer moet ik het formulier inleveren?
mistakes.why: An infinitive after a modal is not split: 'inleveren'.

contrast.dutch: Moet ik het formulier inleveren?
contrast.english: Do I have to submit the form?
contrast.note: Without the question word, a yes/no question remains.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: An indirect question: the content of what you do not know is embedded in a wanneer-clause.

pat-wanneer-11.situationNl: Je staat op een station zonder reisinformatie. Een medewerker vraagt of je weet hoe laat jouw trein er is. Antwoord eerlijk.

clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so 'weet' is second; 'niet' negates the knowledge, and the embedded question follows.

clauses.subject: de trein
clauses.why: The subject 'de trein' comes first and the joined separable verb 'aankomt' closes the clause.

pat-wanneer-11.meaning: I don't know when the train arrives.
pat-wanneer-11.order: The direct question 'Wanneer komt de trein aan?' becomes an embedded question: the subject moves up and the verb to the end.
pat-wanneer-11.forms: weten: ik weet. aankomen: komt aan (direct), aankomt (embedded).
pat-wanneer-11.compare: English 'when the train arrives' keeps its normal order. Dutch moves the verb to the end and joins the particle.

mistakes.wrong: Ik weet niet wanneer komt de trein aan.
mistakes.right: Ik weet niet wanneer de trein aankomt.
mistakes.why: In an embedded question the verb goes to the end and the particle is joined.

mistakes.wrong: Ik weet niet wanneer de trein komt aan.
mistakes.right: Ik weet niet wanneer de trein aankomt.
mistakes.why: The separable verb is written together: 'aankomt'.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer komt de trein aan?
contrast.english: When does the train arrive?
contrast.note: The direct question keeps verb-second order and splits the separable verb.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A polite request embeds the time question after 'kun je me vertellen'.

pat-wanneer-12.situationNl: Je loopt langs een winkel die er al donker uitziet. Vraag een voorbijganger of hij het uur van sluiting kent.

clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: The modal 'Kun' opens the question, then the subject 'je', the object 'me' and the infinitive 'vertellen'.

clauses.subject: de winkel
clauses.why: The subject 'de winkel' comes first and the finite verb 'sluit' closes the clause.

pat-wanneer-12.meaning: Can you tell me when the shop closes?
pat-wanneer-12.order: The main clause is a yes/no request, the embedded question has the verb last. Politeness comes from the frame, not from extra words.
pat-wanneer-12.forms: kunnen: kun je. vertellen: infinitive. sluiten: de winkel sluit.
pat-wanneer-12.compare: English 'Can you tell me when the shop closes' has the same structure. Dutch 'sluit' goes to the end.

mistakes.wrong: Kun je me vertellen wanneer sluit de winkel?
mistakes.right: Kun je me vertellen wanneer de winkel sluit?
mistakes.why: In an embedded question the verb 'sluit' goes last.

mistakes.wrong: Je kunt me vertellen wanneer de winkel sluit?
mistakes.right: Kun je me vertellen wanneer de winkel sluit?
mistakes.why: A request is a yes/no question: 'Kun je' starts it.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer sluit de winkel?
contrast.english: When does the shop close?
contrast.note: The direct question has the verb right after 'wanneer'.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: 'Zich afvragen' (to wonder) introduces an embedded question about a delivery.

pat-wanneer-13.situationNl: Je hebt een pakket besteld dat al dagen onderweg is. Vertel een vriend waar je over piekert.

clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so 'vraag' is second; the reflexive 'me' follows and the particle 'af' ends the main clause.

clauses.subject: de bestelling
clauses.why: The participle 'bezorgd' stands before the finite verb 'wordt', which closes the passive clause.

pat-wanneer-13.meaning: I wonder when the order will be delivered.
pat-wanneer-13.order: 'Zich afvragen' is reflexive and separable: 'vraag me af'. The embedded passive 'bezorgd wordt' has the participle first and 'wordt' last.
pat-wanneer-13.forms: zich afvragen: ik vraag me af. bezorgen > bezorgd. 'Bestelling' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-13.compare: English 'I wonder' is one verb. Dutch uses the reflexive separable 'zich afvragen'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik vraag me af wanneer de bestelling bezorgd.
mistakes.right: Ik vraag me af wanneer de bestelling bezorgd wordt.
mistakes.why: The embedded passive needs its finite verb 'wordt' at the end; the participle 'bezorgd' alone is not a clause.

mistakes.wrong: Ik vraag af me wanneer de bestelling bezorgd wordt.
mistakes.right: Ik vraag me af wanneer de bestelling bezorgd wordt.
mistakes.why: The reflexive 'me' comes before the particle 'af'.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer wordt de bestelling bezorgd?
contrast.english: When will the order be delivered?
contrast.note: The direct question keeps 'wordt' second and the participle at the end.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: 'Bespreken' introduces an embedded question with a modal verb.

pat-wanneer-14.situationNl: Het team wil de nieuwe apparatuur plaatsen, maar de planning is open. Vertel wat jullie op de agenda hebben.

clauses.subject: We
clauses.why: We is first, so 'bespreken' is second and the embedded question follows as its object.

clauses.subject: de installatie
clauses.why: The modal 'kan' stands before its infinitive 'beginnen', and both close the clause behind the subject 'de installatie'.

pat-wanneer-14.meaning: We discuss when the installation can begin.
pat-wanneer-14.order: The embedded question contains a modal chain 'kan beginnen', finite verb first and infinitive last. The main verb 'bespreken' takes the clause as object.
pat-wanneer-14.forms: bespreken: wij bespreken. kunnen: de installatie kan. beginnen: infinitive.
pat-wanneer-14.compare: English 'when the installation can begin' keeps 'can begin' after the subject. Dutch also does, but at the end of the clause.

mistakes.wrong: We bespreken wanneer kan de installatie beginnen.
mistakes.right: We bespreken wanneer de installatie kan beginnen.
mistakes.why: In an embedded question the modal group goes to the end: 'kan beginnen'.

mistakes.wrong: We bespreken wanneer de installatie beginnen kan.
mistakes.right: We bespreken wanneer de installatie kan beginnen.
mistakes.why: The finite modal 'kan' comes before the infinitive in the standard order.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer kan de installatie beginnen?
contrast.english: When can the installation start?
contrast.note: The direct question puts 'kan' right after 'wanneer' and the infinitive at the end.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: The server will finish at a future, unknown moment, so a time clause with 'wanneer' opens the promise.

clauses.subject: de server
clauses.why: The predicate 'klaar' stands before the finite verb 'is', which closes the clause behind 'de server'.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'laat' comes first, then 'ik', the objects 'het je' and the infinitive 'weten'.

pat-wanneer-15.meaning: When the server is ready, I'll let you know.
pat-wanneer-15.order: The fixed pair 'laten weten' keeps 'weten' at the end of the main clause after the inversion 'laat ik'. The clause about the server only supplies the trigger.
pat-wanneer-15.forms: laten weten: ik laat weten. zijn: de server is. 'Server' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-15.compare: English 'I'll let you know' uses 'will'. Dutch says 'laat ik het je weten' in the present, and the verb moves.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de server is klaar, laat ik het je weten.
mistakes.right: Wanneer de server klaar is, laat ik het je weten.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'is' goes behind 'klaar' at the end of the time clause.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de server klaar is, ik laat het je weten.
mistakes.right: Wanneer de server klaar is, laat ik het je weten.
mistakes.why: Behind the comma the main clause starts with 'laat', so the order is 'laat ik'.

contrast.dutch: Ik laat het je weten wanneer de server klaar is.
contrast.english: I'll let you know when the server is ready.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, the subject 'ik' leads and the server clause closes the sentence.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A general rule about what happens after submitting: the time clause names the action that triggers it.

clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: The object 'het formulier' stands before the joined separable verb 'invult', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'krijg' comes first and 'je' follows with the object 'een bevestiging'.

pat-wanneer-16.meaning: When you fill in the form, you get a confirmation.
pat-wanneer-16.order: A statement that is true every time, not an event on one day. The separable verb 'invullen' is written together at the end of the clause.
pat-wanneer-16.forms: invullen: je vult het formulier in (main clause), wanneer je het formulier invult (dependent). 'Bevestiging' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-16.compare: English 'fill in' is a phrasal verb. Dutch joins the particle to the verb in a dependent clause.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer je het formulier vult in, krijg je een bevestiging.
mistakes.right: Wanneer je het formulier invult, krijg je een bevestiging.
mistakes.why: In the time clause 'invullen' is one word: 'invult'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer je het formulier invult, je krijgt een bevestiging.
mistakes.right: Wanneer je het formulier invult, krijg je een bevestiging.
mistakes.why: After the comma the main clause has the verb first: 'krijg je'.

contrast.dutch: Je krijgt een bevestiging wanneer je het formulier invult.
contrast.english: You get a confirmation when you fill in the form.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'je krijgt' keeps the subject in front.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A standing rule for bad weather: 'wanneer' fits a general condition in time.

clauses.subject: het
clauses.why: The dummy subject 'het' comes first and the finite verb 'regent' closes the two-word clause.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'blijven' comes first, then 'we' and the adverb 'binnen'.

pat-wanneer-17.meaning: When it rains, we stay inside.
pat-wanneer-17.order: The shortest possible time clause. The main clause names the rule with the adverb 'binnen' (inside) at the end.
pat-wanneer-17.forms: regenen: het regent. blijven: wij blijven. 'Binnen' is an adverb of place.
pat-wanneer-17.compare: English 'stay inside' is the same shape. Dutch inverts verb and subject after the opening clause.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer het regent, we blijven binnen.
mistakes.right: Wanneer het regent, blijven we binnen.
mistakes.why: After the comma the verb 'blijven' comes first.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer regent het, blijven we binnen.
mistakes.right: Wanneer het regent, blijven we binnen.
mistakes.why: In the time clause the subject 'het' comes before the finite verb 'regent'.

contrast.dutch: We blijven binnen wanneer het regent.
contrast.english: We stay inside when it rains.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, the rule leads and 'regent' ends the sentence.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A habit tied to having free time: the present tense and 'wanneer' express a general condition.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'tijd' stands before the finite verb 'heb', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'ga' comes first, then 'ik' and the infinitive 'hardlopen'.

pat-wanneer-18.meaning: When I have time, I go running.
pat-wanneer-18.order: 'Gaan + infinitive' names an activity you go off to do. The infinitive 'hardlopen' (to run) is a single verb at the end.
pat-wanneer-18.forms: hebben: ik heb. gaan: ik ga. hardlopen: infinitive (one word).
pat-wanneer-18.compare: English 'go running' uses an -ing form. Dutch uses a bare infinitive after 'gaan'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer ik heb tijd, ga ik hardlopen.
mistakes.right: Wanneer ik tijd heb, ga ik hardlopen.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'heb' goes behind the object 'tijd'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer ik tijd heb, ga ik lopen hard.
mistakes.right: Wanneer ik tijd heb, ga ik hardlopen.
mistakes.why: 'Hardlopen' is one word and stays at the end.

contrast.dutch: Ik ga hardlopen wanneer ik tijd heb.
contrast.english: I go running when I have time.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'ik ga hardlopen' leads and 'heb' closes the sentence.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A routine for incoming calls: each time a customer rings, the same step follows.

clauses.subject: de klant
clauses.why: The subject 'de klant' comes first and the finite verb 'belt' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'noteer' comes first, then 'ik' and the object 'zijn vraag'.

pat-wanneer-19.meaning: When the customer calls, I note down his question.
pat-wanneer-19.order: A repeated routine in the present. 'Zijn vraag' (his question) is the object; 'zijn' here is the possessive, not the verb.
pat-wanneer-19.forms: bellen: de klant belt. noteren: ik noteer. 'Vraag' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-19.compare: English 'note down' is a phrasal verb. Dutch 'noteren' is a single verb with a direct object.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de klant belt, ik noteer zijn vraag.
mistakes.right: Wanneer de klant belt, noteer ik zijn vraag.
mistakes.why: The main clause starts with its verb: 'noteer ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de klant telefoon belt, noteer ik zijn vraag.
mistakes.right: Wanneer de klant belt, noteer ik zijn vraag.
mistakes.why: 'Bellen' needs no object here: 'de klant belt'.

contrast.dutch: Ik noteer zijn vraag wanneer de klant belt.
contrast.english: I note down his question when the customer calls.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, the subject 'ik' leads and 'belt' ends the sentence.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: After every restart the same check follows: a repeated routine.

clauses.subject: het systeem
clauses.why: The adverb 'opnieuw' stands between subject and verb; the joined separable verb 'opstart' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'controleer' comes first, then 'ik' and the object 'de logs'.

pat-wanneer-20.meaning: When the system restarts, I check the logs.
pat-wanneer-20.order: 'Opstarten' is separable, but it is written together in the time clause. 'Opnieuw' (again) makes clear this is a restart, not a first start.
pat-wanneer-20.forms: opstarten: het systeem start op / wanneer het systeem opstart. controleren: ik controleer.
pat-wanneer-20.compare: English 'restarts' is a single verb. Dutch uses 'opnieuw opstarten' (start up again).

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer het systeem start opnieuw op, controleer ik de logs.
mistakes.right: Wanneer het systeem opnieuw opstart, controleer ik de logs.
mistakes.why: The separable verb stays whole: 'opstart'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer het systeem opnieuw opstart, ik controleer de logs.
mistakes.right: Wanneer het systeem opnieuw opstart, controleer ik de logs.
mistakes.why: The main clause begins with its verb: 'controleer ik'.

contrast.dutch: Ik controleer de logs wanneer het systeem opnieuw opstart.
contrast.english: I check the logs when the system restarts.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, the routine leads and 'opstart' closes the sentence.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A promise about a future arrival: the host will be waiting at the entrance.

clauses.subject: jullie
clauses.why: The plural subject 'jullie' comes first and the joined plural verb 'aankomen' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'sta' comes first, then 'ik' and the place phrase 'bij de ingang'.

pat-wanneer-21.meaning: When you arrive, I'll be standing at the entrance.
pat-wanneer-21.order: The present 'sta' covers the future, and the plural 'jullie' needs the plural 'aankomen' in the time clause. The place phrase 'bij de ingang' closes the main clause.
pat-wanneer-21.forms: aankomen: jullie komen aan / aankomen. staan: ik sta. 'Ingang' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-21.compare: English 'I'll be standing' uses a future continuous. Dutch uses just 'sta ik'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer jullie komen aan, sta ik bij de ingang.
mistakes.right: Wanneer jullie aankomen, sta ik bij de ingang.
mistakes.why: The separable verb is written together at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer jullie aankomen, ik sta bij de ingang.
mistakes.right: Wanneer jullie aankomen, sta ik bij de ingang.
mistakes.why: The main clause starts with its verb: 'sta ik'.

contrast.dutch: Ik sta bij de ingang wanneer jullie aankomen.
contrast.english: I'll be standing at the entrance when you arrive.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, the promise leads and 'aankomen' closes the sentence.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: Cooking starts every time you get home: a habit expressed with 'wanneer'.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The joined separable verb 'thuiskom' closes this two-word clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'begin' comes first, then 'ik', 'meteen' and the phrase 'met koken'.

pat-wanneer-22.meaning: When I get home, I start cooking right away.
pat-wanneer-22.order: 'Beginnen met' + infinitive is the usual way to say you start doing something. 'Meteen' (right away) stands before the phrase.
pat-wanneer-22.forms: thuiskomen: ik kom thuis / wanneer ik thuiskom. beginnen met: ik begin met koken.
pat-wanneer-22.compare: English 'start cooking' needs no preposition. Dutch needs 'met' before the infinitive.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer ik kom thuis, begin ik meteen met koken.
mistakes.right: Wanneer ik thuiskom, begin ik meteen met koken.
mistakes.why: The separable verb is written together: 'thuiskom'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer ik thuiskom, begin ik meteen koken.
mistakes.right: Wanneer ik thuiskom, begin ik meteen met koken.
mistakes.why: 'Beginnen' needs the preposition 'met' before the infinitive.

contrast.dutch: Ik begin meteen met koken wanneer ik thuiskom.
contrast.english: I start cooking right away when I get home.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, the habit leads and 'thuiskom' ends the sentence.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A general rule about notifications: the trigger is the end of the update.

clauses.subject: de update
clauses.why: 'De update' is the subject; the predicate 'klaar' follows and the finite verb 'is' ends the clause.

clauses.subject: alle gebruikers
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so the plural 'ontvangen' comes first, then 'alle gebruikers' and the object.

pat-wanneer-23.meaning: When the update is ready, all users receive a message.
pat-wanneer-23.order: A plural subject 'alle gebruikers' needs the plural verb 'ontvangen'. The object 'een bericht' ends the sentence.
pat-wanneer-23.forms: ontvangen: zij ontvangen. 'Gebruikers' is plural. 'Bericht' is a het-word, so 'een bericht'.
pat-wanneer-23.compare: English 'receive a message' keeps the same word order. Dutch changes only the verb position around the comma.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de update is klaar, ontvangen alle gebruikers een bericht.
mistakes.right: Wanneer de update klaar is, ontvangen alle gebruikers een bericht.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'is' goes behind 'klaar'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de update klaar is, ontvangt alle gebruikers een bericht.
mistakes.right: Wanneer de update klaar is, ontvangen alle gebruikers een bericht.
mistakes.why: The plural subject 'alle gebruikers' needs the plural verb 'ontvangen'.

contrast.dutch: Alle gebruikers ontvangen een bericht wanneer de update klaar is.
contrast.english: All users receive a message when the update is ready.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'alle gebruikers' leads and 'is' closes the sentence.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A formal instruction to a visitor: pressing the button triggers the test.

clauses.text: Wanneer u op de knop drukt
clauses.subject: u
clauses.why: The phrase 'op de knop' stands before the finite verb 'drukt', which closes the clause; with formal 'u' the verb takes -t.

clauses.subject: de test
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'begint' comes first and the subject 'de test' follows.

pat-wanneer-24.meaning: When you press the button, the test starts.
pat-wanneer-24.order: 'Drukken op' takes the preposition 'op'. The result clause is very short because the test is the only element after the verb.
pat-wanneer-24.forms: drukken: u drukt. beginnen: de test begint. 'Knop' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-24.compare: English 'press the button' has no preposition. Dutch 'drukken op de knop' needs 'op'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer u de knop drukt, begint de test.
mistakes.right: Wanneer u op de knop drukt, begint de test.
mistakes.why: Dutch 'drukken' takes 'op': 'op de knop drukt'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer u op de knop drukt, de test begint.
mistakes.right: Wanneer u op de knop drukt, begint de test.
mistakes.why: The main clause starts with its verb: 'begint de test'.

contrast.dutch: De test begint wanneer u op de knop drukt.
contrast.english: The test starts when you press the button.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'de test' leads and 'drukt' closes the sentence.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: An automatic reaction to darkness: the time clause is the sensor condition.

clauses.subject: het
clauses.why: The predicate 'donker' stands before the finite verb 'wordt', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: de lampen
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so the plural 'gaan' comes first, then 'de lampen', 'automatisch' and the particle 'aan'.

pat-wanneer-25.meaning: When it gets dark, the lights switch on automatically.
pat-wanneer-25.order: 'Aangaan' splits in the main clause: 'gaan ... aan'. The adverb 'automatisch' sits between the subject and the particle.
pat-wanneer-25.forms: aangaan: de lampen gaan aan. worden: het wordt. 'Lamp' is a de-word, plural 'lampen'.
pat-wanneer-25.compare: English 'switch on' is a phrasal verb. Dutch 'aangaan' uses the particle 'aan' at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer het donker wordt, de lampen gaan automatisch aan.
mistakes.right: Wanneer het donker wordt, gaan de lampen automatisch aan.
mistakes.why: After the comma the verb 'gaan' comes first.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer het wordt donker, gaan de lampen automatisch aan.
mistakes.right: Wanneer het donker wordt, gaan de lampen automatisch aan.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'wordt' goes behind the predicate 'donker'.

contrast.dutch: De lampen gaan automatisch aan wanneer het donker wordt.
contrast.english: The lights switch on automatically when it gets dark.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, the subject leads and 'wordt' closes the sentence.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: The host will call the group at a future moment.

clauses.subject: de koffie
clauses.why: 'De koffie' is the subject, the predicate 'klaar' follows it and the finite verb 'is' ends the very short clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'roep' comes first, then 'ik' and the object 'jullie'.

pat-wanneer-26.meaning: When the coffee is ready, I'll call you.
pat-wanneer-26.order: Short and practical: the coffee clause is only subject, predicate and 'is', and the main clause has just verb, subject and the object 'jullie'.
pat-wanneer-26.forms: roepen: ik roep. 'Jullie' is the plural 'you' used as an object here.
pat-wanneer-26.compare: English 'I'll call you' uses 'will'. Dutch uses the present 'roep ik jullie'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de koffie is klaar, roep ik jullie.
mistakes.right: Wanneer de koffie klaar is, roep ik jullie.
mistakes.why: The verb 'is' closes the clause behind the predicate 'klaar', so 'is klaar' in the middle is wrong.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de koffie klaar is, ik roep jullie.
mistakes.right: Wanneer de koffie klaar is, roep ik jullie.
mistakes.why: The main clause starts with its verb: 'roep ik'.

contrast.dutch: Ik roep jullie wanneer de koffie klaar is.
contrast.english: I'll call you when the coffee is ready.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'ik roep jullie' leads and 'is' closes the sentence.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A reporting rule: finding an error triggers an immediate report.

clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: The object 'een fout' stands before the finite verb 'vindt', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'meld' comes first, then 'je', the pronoun 'die' and the adverb 'direct'.

pat-wanneer-27.meaning: When you find an error, you report it straight away.
pat-wanneer-27.order: The pronoun 'die' replaces 'een fout' and stands before the adverb 'direct'. The rule applies every time, and the verb 'meld' is first after the comma.
pat-wanneer-27.forms: vinden: je vindt. melden: je meldt, but after inversion 'meld je'. 'Fout' is a de-word, so 'die'.
pat-wanneer-27.compare: English 'report it' uses 'it'. Dutch uses 'die' because 'fout' is a de-word.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer je een fout vindt, meld je dat direct.
mistakes.right: Wanneer je een fout vindt, meld je die direct.
mistakes.why: 'Fout' is a de-word, so the pronoun is 'die', not 'dat'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer je een fout vindt, je meldt die direct.
mistakes.right: Wanneer je een fout vindt, meld je die direct.
mistakes.why: After the comma the main clause starts with the verb, and the -t disappears: 'meld je'.

contrast.dutch: Meld een fout direct wanneer je die vindt.
contrast.english: Report an error immediately when you find it.
contrast.note: An imperative version states the same rule with 'Meld' as the first word and 'vindt' closing the clause.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: The presentation starts once the group is complete.

clauses.subject: iedereen
clauses.why: The placeholder 'er' stands before the finite verb 'is', which closes the clause behind 'iedereen'.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'beginnen' comes first, then 'we' and the phrase 'met de presentatie'.

pat-wanneer-28.meaning: When everyone is here, we start the presentation.
pat-wanneer-28.order: 'Er zijn' means to be present. The main clause uses 'beginnen met', so the preposition 'met' stands before the noun 'de presentatie'.
pat-wanneer-28.forms: zijn: iedereen is. beginnen: wij beginnen. 'Presentatie' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-28.compare: English 'is here' is a place phrase. Dutch 'er is' is used for being present.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer iedereen is er, beginnen we met de presentatie.
mistakes.right: Wanneer iedereen er is, beginnen we met de presentatie.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'is' goes to the end of the clause, behind 'er'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer iedereen er is, beginnen we de presentatie.
mistakes.right: Wanneer iedereen er is, beginnen we met de presentatie.
mistakes.why: 'Beginnen' needs 'met' before the noun it starts with.

contrast.dutch: We beginnen met de presentatie wanneer iedereen er is.
contrast.english: We start the presentation when everyone is here.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'we beginnen' leads and 'is' closes the sentence.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A standing office rule: closing starts at the beginning of the weekend.

clauses.subject: het weekend
clauses.why: The subject 'het weekend' comes first and the finite verb 'begint' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: we
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'sluiten' comes first, then 'we' and the object 'het kantoor'.

pat-wanneer-29.meaning: When the weekend starts, we close the office.
pat-wanneer-29.order: A fixed weekly rule. Both 'weekend' and 'kantoor' are het-words, so they take 'het'. The main clause is just verb, subject and object.
pat-wanneer-29.forms: beginnen: het weekend begint. sluiten: wij sluiten. 'Kantoor' is a het-word.
pat-wanneer-29.compare: English 'starts' is the same verb. Dutch changes only the verb positions: 'begint' goes last in the time clause, 'sluiten' first in the main clause.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer het weekend begint, we sluiten het kantoor.
mistakes.right: Wanneer het weekend begint, sluiten we het kantoor.
mistakes.why: After the comma the verb 'sluiten' comes first.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer het begint weekend, sluiten we het kantoor.
mistakes.right: Wanneer het weekend begint, sluiten we het kantoor.
mistakes.why: The subject 'het weekend' comes before the verb 'begint'.

contrast.dutch: We sluiten het kantoor wanneer het weekend begint.
contrast.english: We close the office when the weekend starts.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, 'we sluiten' leads and 'begint' closes the sentence.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A callback promise: the results are the condition, and you will phone back afterwards.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'de resultaten' stands before the finite verb 'heb', which closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The time clause fills the first slot, so 'bel' comes first, then 'ik', the object 'je' and the particle 'terug'.

pat-wanneer-30.meaning: When I have the results, I'll call you back.
pat-wanneer-30.order: 'Terugbellen' splits in the main clause: 'bel ... terug'. The object 'je' stands between verb and particle, so the sentence ends on the particle.
pat-wanneer-30.forms: terugbellen: ik bel terug. hebben: ik heb. 'Resultaat' is a het-word, plural 'resultaten'.
pat-wanneer-30.compare: English 'call back' keeps 'back' next to the verb. Dutch puts 'terug' at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer ik heb de resultaten, bel ik je terug.
mistakes.right: Wanneer ik de resultaten heb, bel ik je terug.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'heb' goes behind the object at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer ik de resultaten heb, bel ik terugbellen je.
mistakes.right: Wanneer ik de resultaten heb, bel ik je terug.
mistakes.why: 'Terugbellen' splits in a main clause: 'bel ik je terug'.

contrast.dutch: Ik bel je terug wanneer ik de resultaten heb.
contrast.english: I'll call you back when I have the results.
contrast.note: With the main clause first, the promise leads and 'heb' closes the sentence.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: The callback comes after a future moment, so 'wanneer' ends the sentence with its verb.

clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so 'bel' is second; 'je' is the object and the particle 'terug' finishes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'de resultaten' stands before the finite verb 'heb', which closes the time clause.

pat-wanneer-31.meaning: I'll call you back when I have the results.
pat-wanneer-31.order: The promise leads, the condition follows. The main clause keeps ordinary order, so only the time clause sends its verb to the end.
pat-wanneer-31.forms: terugbellen: ik bel je terug. hebben: ik heb. The same fact appears with the time clause first in another card.
pat-wanneer-31.compare: English 'call you back when I have' is the same order of ideas. Dutch moves 'heb' to the end and splits 'terugbellen'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik bel je terug wanneer heb ik de resultaten.
mistakes.right: Ik bel je terug wanneer ik de resultaten heb.
mistakes.why: In a time clause the subject 'ik' comes before the verb 'heb'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik terugbel je wanneer ik de resultaten heb.
mistakes.right: Ik bel je terug wanneer ik de resultaten heb.
mistakes.why: In the main clause 'terugbellen' splits: 'bel ... terug'.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer ik de resultaten heb, bel ik je terug.
contrast.english: When I have the results, I'll call you back.
contrast.note: With the time clause first, 'bel ik je terug' is inverted.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: The celebration is planned for a future moment: the completion of the project.

clauses.subject: We
clauses.why: We is first, so 'vieren' is second and 'het' is the object that stands for the finished project.

clauses.subject: het project
clauses.why: The predicate 'klaar' stands before the finite verb 'is', which closes the clause behind 'het project'.

pat-wanneer-32.meaning: We'll celebrate when the project is finished.
pat-wanneer-32.order: 'Het' in the main clause points to the finished project. The time clause names the occasion and ends with 'is'.
pat-wanneer-32.forms: vieren: wij vieren. zijn: het project is. 'Project' is a het-word.
pat-wanneer-32.compare: English 'celebrate it' needs an object too. Dutch uses 'het' before the time clause.

mistakes.wrong: We vieren het wanneer het project is klaar.
mistakes.right: We vieren het wanneer het project klaar is.
mistakes.why: The verb 'is' goes behind 'klaar' at the end.

mistakes.wrong: We het vieren wanneer het project klaar is.
mistakes.right: We vieren het wanneer het project klaar is.
mistakes.why: In the main clause the verb is second: 'vieren we het'. With the subject first it is 'We vieren het'.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer het project klaar is, vieren we het.
contrast.english: When the project is finished, we'll celebrate it.
contrast.note: Time clause first: 'vieren we het' is inverted.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A visit planned for any moment she is in the area: an open future condition.

clauses.subject: Zij
clauses.why: Zij is first, so 'komt' is second and the particle 'langs' ends the main clause.

clauses.text: wanneer ze in de buurt is
clauses.subject: ze
clauses.why: The place phrase 'in de buurt' stands before the finite verb 'is', which closes the clause.

pat-wanneer-33.meaning: She drops by when she is in the area.
pat-wanneer-33.order: 'Langskomen' splits in the main clause: 'komt ... langs'. The time clause adds the open condition with 'ze', the unstressed 'zij'.
pat-wanneer-33.forms: langskomen: zij komt langs. zijn: ze is. 'In de buurt' = in the neighbourhood.
pat-wanneer-33.compare: English 'drops by' is a phrasal verb. Dutch uses the separable verb 'langskomen'.

mistakes.wrong: Zij langskomt wanneer ze in de buurt is.
mistakes.right: Zij komt langs wanneer ze in de buurt is.
mistakes.why: In a main clause 'langskomen' splits: 'komt ... langs'.

mistakes.wrong: Zij komt langs wanneer ze is in de buurt.
mistakes.right: Zij komt langs wanneer ze in de buurt is.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'is' goes behind the phrase 'in de buurt'.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer ze in de buurt is, komt zij langs.
contrast.english: When she is in the area, she drops by.
contrast.note: Time clause first: 'komt zij langs' is inverted.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A wish tied to the end of today's work.

clauses.subject: Hij
clauses.why: Hij is first, so the modal 'wil' is second and the infinitive 'rusten' closes the main clause.

clauses.subject: hij
clauses.why: 'Vandaag' and the predicate 'klaar' stand before the finite verb 'is', which closes the clause.

pat-wanneer-34.meaning: He wants to rest when he is done today.
pat-wanneer-34.order: A modal chain 'wil rusten' in the main clause. 'Vandaag' belongs to the time clause and sits before 'klaar', so 'is' closes the sentence.
pat-wanneer-34.forms: willen: hij wil. rusten: infinitive. 'Klaar zijn' = to be done.
pat-wanneer-34.compare: English 'wants to rest' keeps 'to'. Dutch needs no 'te' after the modal 'wil'.

mistakes.wrong: Hij wil te rusten wanneer hij vandaag klaar is.
mistakes.right: Hij wil rusten wanneer hij vandaag klaar is.
mistakes.why: The modal 'wil' takes a bare infinitive, so 'rusten' stands without 'te' in front of it.

mistakes.wrong: Hij wil rusten wanneer hij is vandaag klaar.
mistakes.right: Hij wil rusten wanneer hij vandaag klaar is.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'is' goes to the end of the time clause.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer hij vandaag klaar is, wil hij rusten.
contrast.english: When he is done today, he wants to rest.
contrast.note: Time clause first: 'wil hij rusten' is inverted.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: Permission depends on a future moment: everyone being present.

clauses.subject: Je
clauses.why: Je is first, so the modal 'mag' is second and the infinitive 'beginnen' closes the main clause.

clauses.subject: iedereen
clauses.why: The predicate 'aanwezig' stands before the finite verb 'is', which closes the clause.

pat-wanneer-35.meaning: You may start when everyone is present.
pat-wanneer-35.order: The permission 'mag beginnen' leads and the condition follows. In the time clause the predicate 'aanwezig' precedes the finite verb 'is'.
pat-wanneer-35.forms: mogen: je mag. beginnen: infinitive. 'Aanwezig zijn' = to be present.
pat-wanneer-35.compare: English 'may start' is the same. Dutch has the verb pair 'mag beginnen' at the end of the main clause.

mistakes.wrong: Je mag beginnen wanneer iedereen is aanwezig.
mistakes.right: Je mag beginnen wanneer iedereen aanwezig is.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'is' goes behind 'aanwezig'.

mistakes.wrong: Je mag beginnen wanneer iedereen aanwezig zijn.
mistakes.right: Je mag beginnen wanneer iedereen aanwezig is.
mistakes.why: 'Iedereen' takes the singular verb 'is', never the plural 'zijn'.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer iedereen aanwezig is, mag je beginnen.
contrast.english: When everyone is present, you may start.
contrast.note: Time clause first: 'mag je beginnen' is inverted.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A general rule for a safety system: the alarm responds to a rising temperature.

clauses.subject: Het alarm
clauses.why: 'Het alarm' is first, so 'gaat' is second and the particle 'af' closes the main clause.

clauses.text: wanneer de temperatuur te hoog wordt
clauses.subject: de temperatuur
clauses.why: The phrase 'te hoog' stands before the finite verb 'wordt', which closes the clause.

pat-wanneer-36.meaning: The alarm goes off when the temperature gets too high.
pat-wanneer-36.order: 'Afgaan' splits in the main clause. In the time clause 'te hoog' (too high) is the predicate, and 'worden' expresses the change.
pat-wanneer-36.forms: afgaan: het alarm gaat af. worden: de temperatuur wordt. 'Temperatuur' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-36.compare: English 'gets too high' uses 'get' for the change. Dutch uses 'wordt te hoog', and the verb 'wordt' goes to the very end of the clause.

mistakes.wrong: Het alarm gaat af wanneer de temperatuur wordt te hoog.
mistakes.right: Het alarm gaat af wanneer de temperatuur te hoog wordt.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'wordt' goes behind 'te hoog'.

mistakes.wrong: Het alarm afgaat wanneer de temperatuur te hoog wordt.
mistakes.right: Het alarm gaat af wanneer de temperatuur te hoog wordt.
mistakes.why: In a main clause 'afgaan' splits: 'gaat ... af'.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer de temperatuur te hoog wordt, gaat het alarm af.
contrast.english: When the temperature gets too high, the alarm goes off.
contrast.note: Time clause first: 'gaat het alarm af' is inverted.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: An invoicing rule: payment arrival triggers the invoice.

clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so 'stuur' is second and the object 'de factuur' follows.

clauses.subject: de betaling
clauses.why: The particle 'binnen' stands before the finite verb 'is', which closes the clause behind 'de betaling'.

pat-wanneer-37.meaning: I send the invoice when the payment is in.
pat-wanneer-37.order: 'Binnen zijn' means to have arrived (of money). The predicate comes before the verb at the end of the time clause.
pat-wanneer-37.forms: sturen: ik stuur. zijn: de betaling is. 'Factuur' and 'betaling' are de-words.
pat-wanneer-37.compare: English 'is in' is a phrasal state. Dutch says the payment 'is binnen'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik stuur de factuur wanneer de betaling is binnen.
mistakes.right: Ik stuur de factuur wanneer de betaling binnen is.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'is' goes behind 'binnen'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik de factuur stuur wanneer de betaling binnen is.
mistakes.right: Ik stuur de factuur wanneer de betaling binnen is.
mistakes.why: In the main clause the verb is second: 'Ik stuur de factuur'.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer de betaling binnen is, stuur ik de factuur.
contrast.english: When the payment is in, I send the invoice.
contrast.note: Time clause first: 'stuur ik de factuur' is inverted.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: Users may sign in once access has been granted.

clauses.subject: De gebruikers
clauses.why: 'De gebruikers' is first, so the plural 'loggen' is second and the particle 'in' closes the main clause.

clauses.subject: ze
clauses.why: The object 'toegang' stands before the perfect group 'hebben gekregen', in which the finite 'hebben' comes first.

pat-wanneer-38.meaning: The users log in when they have been given access.
pat-wanneer-38.order: A perfect inside the time clause shows that access comes first. The perfect group ends the clause: 'hebben gekregen'.
pat-wanneer-38.forms: inloggen: zij loggen in. krijgen > gekregen. 'Toegang' = access (no article).
pat-wanneer-38.compare: English 'have been given' is a passive perfect. Dutch says 'hebben gekregen' (have received).

mistakes.wrong: De gebruikers loggen in wanneer ze toegang gekregen hebben ze.
mistakes.right: De gebruikers loggen in wanneer ze toegang hebben gekregen.
mistakes.why: The pronoun 'ze' stands at the front of the clause, before 'toegang'.

mistakes.wrong: De gebruikers loggen in wanneer ze hebben toegang gekregen.
mistakes.right: De gebruikers loggen in wanneer ze toegang hebben gekregen.
mistakes.why: The object 'toegang' goes before the perfect group at the end.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer ze toegang hebben gekregen, loggen de gebruikers in.
contrast.english: When they have been given access, the users log in.
contrast.note: Time clause first: 'loggen de gebruikers in' is inverted.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: Preparation depends on knowing the figures: a sequence in your work routine.

clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so 'bereid' is second; the object 'de presentatie' follows and the particle 'voor' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: The object 'de cijfers' stands before the finite verb 'ken', which closes the clause.

pat-wanneer-39.meaning: I prepare the presentation when I know the figures.
pat-wanneer-39.order: 'Voorbereiden' splits in the main clause: 'bereid ... voor'. The time clause is short and uses 'kennen' for being familiar with the figures.
pat-wanneer-39.forms: voorbereiden: ik bereid voor. kennen: ik ken. 'Cijfers' is plural.
pat-wanneer-39.compare: English 'prepare' has no particle. Dutch 'voorbereiden' puts 'voor' at the end of the clause.

mistakes.wrong: Ik bereid voor de presentatie wanneer ik de cijfers ken.
mistakes.right: Ik bereid de presentatie voor wanneer ik de cijfers ken.
mistakes.why: The particle 'voor' goes to the end of the main clause, behind the object.

mistakes.wrong: Ik bereid de presentatie voor wanneer ik ken de cijfers.
mistakes.right: Ik bereid de presentatie voor wanneer ik de cijfers ken.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'ken' goes behind the object in the time clause.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer ik de cijfers ken, bereid ik de presentatie voor.
contrast.english: When I know the figures, I prepare the presentation.
contrast.note: Time clause first: 'bereid ik de presentatie voor' is inverted.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: An offer of availability: reach me at any moment you need me.

clauses.subject: Je
clauses.why: Je is first, so the modal 'kunt' is second; the object 'me' follows and the infinitive 'bereiken' closes the clause.

clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: The object 'me' and the predicate 'nodig' stand before the finite verb 'hebt', which closes the clause.

pat-wanneer-40.meaning: You can reach me when you need me.
pat-wanneer-40.order: 'Nodig hebben' (to need) is a fixed pair, and in the time clause the verb 'hebt' ends after 'nodig'. The first 'me' belongs to the main clause.
pat-wanneer-40.forms: kunnen: je kunt. bereiken: infinitive. nodig hebben: je hebt me nodig.
pat-wanneer-40.compare: English 'need me' is a single verb. Dutch splits it as 'me nodig hebt'.

mistakes.wrong: Je kunt me bereiken wanneer je me hebt nodig.
mistakes.right: Je kunt me bereiken wanneer je me nodig hebt.
mistakes.why: The predicate 'nodig' goes before the finite verb 'hebt'.

mistakes.wrong: Je kunt bereiken me wanneer je me nodig hebt.
mistakes.right: Je kunt me bereiken wanneer je me nodig hebt.
mistakes.why: In the main clause the object 'me' goes before the final infinitive 'bereiken'.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer je me nodig hebt, kun je me bereiken.
contrast.english: When you need me, you can reach me.
contrast.note: Time clause first: 'kun je me bereiken' is inverted.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: The backup runs at a fixed future time: the closing of the office.

clauses.subject: We
clauses.why: We is first, so 'starten' is second and the object 'de back-up' follows.

clauses.subject: het kantoor
clauses.why: The subject 'het kantoor' comes first and the finite verb 'sluit' closes the clause.

pat-wanneer-41.meaning: We start the backup when the office closes.
pat-wanneer-41.order: A scheduled routine: the main clause names the action and the time clause names the trigger, so 'sluit' ends the sentence after 'het kantoor'.
pat-wanneer-41.forms: starten: wij starten. sluiten: het kantoor sluit. 'Back-up' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-41.compare: English 'start the backup' is the same. Dutch sends 'sluit' to the end of the time clause.

mistakes.wrong: We starten de back-up wanneer sluit het kantoor.
mistakes.right: We starten de back-up wanneer het kantoor sluit.
mistakes.why: In the time clause the verb 'sluit' comes after the subject.

mistakes.wrong: We de back-up starten wanneer het kantoor sluit.
mistakes.right: We starten de back-up wanneer het kantoor sluit.
mistakes.why: In the main clause the verb is second: 'We starten de back-up'.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer het kantoor sluit, starten we de back-up.
contrast.english: When the office closes, we start the backup.
contrast.note: Time clause first: 'starten we de back-up' is inverted.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A habit tied to leaving: she closes the door each time.

clauses.subject: Zij
clauses.why: Zij is first, so 'sluit' is second and the object 'de deur' follows.

clauses.subject: ze
clauses.why: The joined separable verb 'weggaat' closes this short clause.

pat-wanneer-42.meaning: She closes the door when she leaves.
pat-wanneer-42.order: The separable verb 'weggaan' is written together in the time clause. Both clauses share one person: 'zij' and the unstressed 'ze'.
pat-wanneer-42.forms: sluiten: zij sluit. weggaan: ze gaat weg / wanneer ze weggaat.
pat-wanneer-42.compare: English 'goes away' keeps 'away' separate. Dutch glues 'weg' to the verb in the dependent clause.

mistakes.wrong: Zij sluit de deur wanneer ze gaat weg.
mistakes.right: Zij sluit de deur wanneer ze weggaat.
mistakes.why: The separable verb is written together: 'weggaat'.

mistakes.wrong: Zij de deur sluit wanneer ze weggaat.
mistakes.right: Zij sluit de deur wanneer ze weggaat.
mistakes.why: In the main clause the verb is second: 'sluit de deur'.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer ze weggaat, sluit zij de deur.
contrast.english: When she leaves, she closes the door.
contrast.note: Time clause first: 'sluit zij de deur' is inverted.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: Taking a coat when rain is about to start: a habit with a future-oriented clause.

clauses.subject: Ik
clauses.why: Ik is first, so 'pak' is second and the object 'mijn jas' follows.

clauses.subject: het
clauses.why: The verb group 'gaat regenen' closes the clause: the finite 'gaat' is followed by the infinitive 'regenen'.

pat-wanneer-43.meaning: I take my coat when it's going to rain.
pat-wanneer-43.order: 'Gaan + infinitive' expresses what is about to happen. The time clause ends on the infinitive 'regenen', after the finite 'gaat'.
pat-wanneer-43.forms: pakken: ik pak. gaan regenen: het gaat regenen. 'Jas' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-43.compare: English 'is going to rain' uses a similar future form. Dutch has 'gaat regenen' at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Ik pak mijn jas wanneer het regenen gaat.
mistakes.right: Ik pak mijn jas wanneer het gaat regenen.
mistakes.why: The finite verb 'gaat' comes before the infinitive 'regenen'.

mistakes.wrong: Ik pak mijn jas wanneer het gaat te regenen.
mistakes.right: Ik pak mijn jas wanneer het gaat regenen.
mistakes.why: After 'gaan' the infinitive is bare: no 'te'.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer het gaat regenen, pak ik mijn jas.
contrast.english: When it's going to rain, I take my coat.
contrast.note: Time clause first: 'pak ik mijn jas' is inverted.

sense.label: wanneer = when (time clause)
sense.why: A timetable rule: departure depends on the driver being ready.

clauses.subject: De bus
clauses.why: 'De bus' is first, so 'vertrekt' is second and the main clause is complete.

clauses.subject: de chauffeur
clauses.why: The predicate 'klaar' stands before the finite verb 'is', which closes the clause behind 'de chauffeur'.

pat-wanneer-44.meaning: The bus leaves when the driver is ready.
pat-wanneer-44.order: A short main clause followed by a time clause. The bus has no fixed hour: its departure depends on the driver, so 'is' ends the sentence.
pat-wanneer-44.forms: vertrekken: de bus vertrekt. zijn: de chauffeur is. 'Chauffeur' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-44.compare: English 'is ready' keeps 'is' next to the subject. Dutch puts it behind 'klaar'.

mistakes.wrong: De bus vertrekt wanneer de chauffeur is klaar.
mistakes.right: De bus vertrekt wanneer de chauffeur klaar is.
mistakes.why: Inside 'wanneer de chauffeur klaar is' the verb 'is' closes the clause, not the slot before 'klaar'.

mistakes.wrong: De bus wanneer de chauffeur klaar is vertrekt.
mistakes.right: De bus vertrekt wanneer de chauffeur klaar is.
mistakes.why: The time clause comes after the verb 'vertrekt' in this sentence.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer de chauffeur klaar is, vertrekt de bus.
contrast.english: When the driver is ready, the bus leaves.
contrast.note: Time clause first: 'vertrekt de bus' is inverted.

sense.label: wanneer = when (question word)
sense.why: A direct question asking for the time of a visit; 'wanneer' is the question word, not a conjunction.

pat-wanneer-45.situationNl: Je verwarming valt al dagen uit en er is een afspraak gemaakt. Informeer bij de dienst naar het bezoekmoment van de technicus.

clauses.subject: de monteur
clauses.why: 'Wanneer' opens the question, so the finite verb 'komt' is second, then 'de monteur', and the particle 'langs' ends the clause.

pat-wanneer-45.meaning: When is the technician coming by?
pat-wanneer-45.order: Question word, verb, subject, particle. The separable verb 'langskomen' splits, with 'langs' left at the very end of the question.
pat-wanneer-45.forms: langskomen: de monteur komt langs. 'Monteur' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-45.compare: English 'coming by' keeps 'by' next to the verb. Dutch puts 'langs' at the end of the clause.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de monteur komt langs?
mistakes.right: Wanneer komt de monteur langs?
mistakes.why: The verb must follow the question word directly: 'Wanneer komt de monteur'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer langskomt de monteur?
mistakes.right: Wanneer komt de monteur langs?
mistakes.why: In a direct question the separable verb splits: 'komt ... langs'.

contrast.dutch: Weet u wanneer de monteur langskomt?
contrast.english: Do you know when the technician is coming by?
contrast.note: Embedded after 'weet u', the separable verb is joined and goes last.

sense.label: wanneer = when (question word)
sense.why: A short direct question with 'zijn' about the next meeting.

pat-wanneer-46.situationNl: Je hebt de laatste uitnodiging gemist. Vraag je collega naar de datum van het volgende overleg.

clauses.subject: de volgende vergadering
clauses.why: 'Wanneer' opens the question, so 'is' is second and the subject 'de volgende vergadering' follows it.

pat-wanneer-46.order: The simplest question shape: question word, 'is', then the subject 'de volgende vergadering'. The adjective 'volgende' takes -e before a de-word.
pat-wanneer-46.compare: English 'When is the next meeting?' has the same order. Dutch never adds an auxiliary.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de volgende vergadering is?
mistakes.right: Wanneer is de volgende vergadering?
mistakes.why: The verb 'is' comes right behind 'wanneer'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer is de volgend vergadering?
mistakes.right: Wanneer is de volgende vergadering?
mistakes.why: After 'de' the adjective takes -e: 'volgende'.

contrast.dutch: Ik vraag me af wanneer de volgende vergadering is.
contrast.english: I wonder when the next meeting is.
contrast.note: In the embedded version 'is' goes to the end.

sense.label: wanneer = when (question word)
sense.why: A direct question with a time adverb at the end.

pat-wanneer-47.situationNl: Je moet nog iets afhandelen op een andere afdeling. Vraag naar het uur waarop het gebouw dichtgaat.

clauses.subject: het kantoor
clauses.why: 'Wanneer' opens the question, so 'sluit' is second, then the subject 'het kantoor', and 'vandaag' ends it.

pat-wanneer-47.meaning: When does the office close today?
pat-wanneer-47.order: Dutch can put the day word 'vandaag' at the end of a question. The verb 'sluit' stays directly after 'wanneer' and the subject follows it.
pat-wanneer-47.compare: English 'does ... close today' needs 'does' and keeps 'today' last. Dutch also ends on 'vandaag', but needs no auxiliary.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer het kantoor sluit vandaag?
mistakes.right: Wanneer sluit het kantoor vandaag?
mistakes.why: The finite verb follows 'wanneer' directly.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer sluit vandaag het kantoor?
mistakes.right: Wanneer sluit het kantoor vandaag?
mistakes.why: The subject 'het kantoor' stands before the time adverb 'vandaag'.

contrast.dutch: Het kantoor sluit vandaag om vijf uur.
contrast.english: The office closes at five o'clock today.
contrast.note: The answer is a statement with the verb second and a time phrase.

sense.label: wanneer = when (question word)
sense.why: A direct question with a modal: 'kan' follows 'wanneer'.

pat-wanneer-48.situationNl: Je wilt een collega spreken maar hij zit voortdurend in overleg. Vraag naar zijn beschikbaarheid voor een telefoontje.

clauses.subject: ik
clauses.why: 'Wanneer' opens the question, so the modal 'kan' is second, followed by 'ik', the object 'je' and the infinitive 'bellen'.

pat-wanneer-48.order: The modal 'kan' sits next to the question word, and the infinitive 'bellen' goes to the very end, after the object 'je'.
pat-wanneer-48.forms: kunnen: ik kan. bellen: infinitive. 'Je' is the unstressed object.
pat-wanneer-48.compare: English 'can I call you' has the same sequence. Dutch has the same too, with a different spelling of the pronoun.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer ik kan je bellen?
mistakes.right: Wanneer kan ik je bellen?
mistakes.why: 'Kan' stands directly behind 'wanneer', before the subject 'ik', in a direct question.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer kan ik bellen je?
mistakes.right: Wanneer kan ik je bellen?
mistakes.why: The object 'je' goes before the infinitive 'bellen'.

contrast.dutch: Kan ik je bellen?
contrast.english: Can I call you?
contrast.note: Without a question word it is a yes/no question.

sense.label: wanneer = when (question word)
sense.why: A direct question about free time with 'hebben'.

pat-wanneer-49.situationNl: Je hebt een korte vraag over je taken. Vraag je collega naar een gaatje in zijn dag.

clauses.text: Wanneer heb je tijd voor een kort gesprek
clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: 'Wanneer' opens the question, so 'heb' is second, then 'je', the object 'tijd' and the phrase 'voor een kort gesprek'.

pat-wanneer-49.meaning: When do you have time for a short talk?
pat-wanneer-49.order: 'Tijd hebben voor' takes the preposition 'voor'. The object 'tijd' stands before the purpose phrase, so the question ends on 'gesprek'.
pat-wanneer-49.forms: hebben: je hebt becomes 'heb je' after inversion. 'Gesprek' is a het-word, so 'een kort gesprek'.
pat-wanneer-49.compare: English 'do you have time' needs 'do'. Dutch uses 'heb je' directly after the question word.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer je hebt tijd voor een kort gesprek?
mistakes.right: Wanneer heb je tijd voor een kort gesprek?
mistakes.why: The verb 'heb' comes directly after 'wanneer'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer heb je tijd voor een kort gesprekken?
mistakes.right: Wanneer heb je tijd voor een kort gesprek?
mistakes.why: 'Een kort gesprek' is singular; a plural 'gesprekken' after 'een' is wrong.

contrast.dutch: Heb je tijd voor een kort gesprek?
contrast.english: Do you have time for a short talk?
contrast.note: Without 'wanneer', the question begins with 'heb' and asks only whether time exists, not when.

sense.label: wanneer = when (question word)
sense.why: A direct question with 'zijn' about completion.

pat-wanneer-50.situationNl: De nieuwe versie wordt al uren geïnstalleerd. Vraag naar het verwachte einde van de installatie.

clauses.subject: de update
clauses.why: 'Wanneer' opens the question, so 'is' is second, then the subject 'de update' and the predicate 'klaar'.

pat-wanneer-50.meaning: When will the update be ready?
pat-wanneer-50.order: Question word, 'is', subject, predicate. The present tense asks about a future moment, and 'klaar' ends the question.
pat-wanneer-50.forms: zijn: de update is. 'Klaar' is the predicate.
pat-wanneer-50.compare: English 'will be ready' marks the future with 'will'. Dutch uses the present 'is'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de update is klaar?
mistakes.right: Wanneer is de update klaar?
mistakes.why: The verb 'is' comes directly after 'wanneer'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer klaar is de update?
mistakes.right: Wanneer is de update klaar?
mistakes.why: The subject goes before the predicate: 'is de update klaar'.

contrast.dutch: De update is vanavond klaar.
contrast.english: The update is ready tonight.
contrast.note: The answer is a statement: subject, verb, time and predicate.

sense.label: wanneer = when (question word)
sense.why: A direct question with 'gaan' about holiday plans.

pat-wanneer-51.situationNl: Buren praten over de zomer en hun koffers staan al bijna klaar. Vraag naar de dag van hun vertrek.

clauses.subject: jullie
clauses.why: 'Wanneer' opens the question, so the plural 'gaan' is second, then 'jullie' and the phrase 'op vakantie'.

pat-wanneer-51.meaning: When are you going on holiday?
pat-wanneer-51.order: The destination-like phrase 'op vakantie' ends the question. The verb 'gaan' is plural to match 'jullie' and stands next to 'wanneer'.
pat-wanneer-51.forms: gaan: jullie gaan. 'Op vakantie gaan' = to go on holiday.
pat-wanneer-51.compare: English 'are you going' uses a continuous. Dutch uses the plain present 'gaan jullie'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer jullie gaan op vakantie?
mistakes.right: Wanneer gaan jullie op vakantie?
mistakes.why: The finite verb follows the question word.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer gaat jullie op vakantie?
mistakes.right: Wanneer gaan jullie op vakantie?
mistakes.why: The plural 'jullie' needs the plural verb 'gaan'.

contrast.dutch: Gaan jullie op vakantie?
contrast.english: Are you going on holiday?
contrast.note: Without 'wanneer', the question starts with 'gaan' and asks whether the trip happens, not when.

sense.label: wanneer = when (question word)
sense.why: A formal question about a past moment: 'hebt' with the participle.

pat-wanneer-52.situationNl: Je onderzoekt een klacht van een klant en spreekt een collega formeel aan. Vraag naar het moment van binnenkomst van het bericht.

clauses.text: Wanneer hebt u de klacht ontvangen
clauses.subject: u
clauses.why: 'Wanneer' opens the question, so the auxiliary 'hebt' is second, then the formal 'u', the object and the participle 'ontvangen'.

pat-wanneer-52.meaning: When did you receive the complaint?
pat-wanneer-52.order: A formal perfect-tense question. The auxiliary 'hebt' leads and the participle 'ontvangen' ends the question, with 'u' and the object between them.
pat-wanneer-52.forms: hebben: u hebt. ontvangen: participle equals infinitive. 'Klacht' is a de-word.
pat-wanneer-52.compare: English 'did you receive' uses the simple past. Dutch usually asks with the perfect: 'hebt u ontvangen'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer u hebt de klacht ontvangen?
mistakes.right: Wanneer hebt u de klacht ontvangen?
mistakes.why: The auxiliary 'hebt' comes directly after 'wanneer'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer hebt u de klacht geontvangen?
mistakes.right: Wanneer hebt u de klacht ontvangen?
mistakes.why: The prefix ont- takes no ge-: 'ontvangen'.

contrast.dutch: Wanneer heb je de klacht ontvangen?
contrast.english: When did you receive the complaint?
contrast.note: With the informal 'je' the auxiliary becomes 'heb'.

sense.label: wanneer = when (question word)
sense.why: A direct question about the start of a training.

pat-wanneer-53.situationNl: Je begeleidt iemand die net is begonnen. Vraag naar de startdag van de inwerpcursus voor beginners.

clauses.text: Wanneer begint de training voor nieuwe collega's
clauses.subject: de training
clauses.why: 'Wanneer' opens the question, so 'begint' is second, then the subject 'de training' and the purpose phrase 'voor nieuwe collega's'.

pat-wanneer-53.meaning: When does the training for new colleagues start?
pat-wanneer-53.order: The phrase 'voor nieuwe collega's' describes the training and stays right behind it. The plural 'collega's' takes an apostrophe.
pat-wanneer-53.forms: beginnen: de training begint. 'Training' is a de-word; 'collega's' is the plural of 'collega'.
pat-wanneer-53.compare: English 'for new colleagues' also follows the noun. Dutch needs no 'does'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer de training begint voor nieuwe collega's?
mistakes.right: Wanneer begint de training voor nieuwe collega's?
mistakes.why: The verb 'begint' follows 'wanneer' directly.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer begint de training voor nieuwe collegas?
mistakes.right: Wanneer begint de training voor nieuwe collega's?
mistakes.why: The plural of 'collega' is written with an apostrophe: 'collega's'.

contrast.dutch: De training begint maandag.
contrast.english: The training starts on Monday.
contrast.note: A statement answers the question with verb second.

sense.label: wanneer = when (question word)
sense.why: A passive direct question about a delivery.

pat-wanneer-54.situationNl: Je volgt een bestelling die al dagen onderweg is. Vraag de koerier naar het levermoment.

clauses.subject: het pakket
clauses.why: 'Wanneer' opens the question, so 'wordt' is second, then the subject 'het pakket' and the participle 'bezorgd'.

pat-wanneer-54.meaning: When will the package be delivered?
pat-wanneer-54.order: A passive in the direct question: auxiliary after the question word, participle at the end. Who delivers it is not mentioned.
pat-wanneer-54.forms: worden: het pakket wordt. bezorgen > bezorgd. 'Pakket' is a het-word.
pat-wanneer-54.compare: English 'will be delivered' has two auxiliaries. Dutch uses 'wordt bezorgd'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer het pakket wordt bezorgd?
mistakes.right: Wanneer wordt het pakket bezorgd?
mistakes.why: The auxiliary 'wordt' comes directly after 'wanneer'.

mistakes.wrong: Wanneer wordt het pakket gebezorgd?
mistakes.right: Wanneer wordt het pakket bezorgd?
mistakes.why: 'Bezorgen' has the inseparable prefix be-, so no ge-: 'bezorgd'.

contrast.dutch: Het pakket wordt morgen bezorgd.
contrast.english: The package will be delivered tomorrow.
contrast.note: The statement version puts the subject first.

sense.label: wanneer = when (question word)
sense.why: A perfect-tense question about the closing of a ticket.

pat-wanneer-55.situationNl: Een klant betwist de afhandeling van zijn melding. Vraag je collega naar het tijdstip waarop de zaak is afgesloten.

clauses.text: Wanneer heb je het ticket gesloten
clauses.subject: je
clauses.why: 'Wanneer' opens the question, so 'heb' is second, then 'je', the object and the participle 'gesloten'.

pat-wanneer-55.meaning: When did you close the ticket?
pat-wanneer-55.order: The perfect group is split around the object: 'heb ... gesloten'. 'Ticket' is a het-word, and the participle ends the question.
pat-wanneer-55.forms: sluiten > gesloten. hebben: je hebt becomes 'heb je' after inversion.
